fields.v: Jureczka, M., Paleczek, A., Campbell, A., Przystalski, K. (2026). BDD-Bench: A Behavior-Driven Benchmark for Coding Agents across the Application Lifecycle. In: Proceedings of the 1st International Workshop on Agentic AI for Next-Generation Software Development (AgenticDev '26), Munich, Germany, pp. 32-41. ACM. https://doi.org/10.1145/3843282.3844426
Workshop — AgenticDev '26 (1st International Workshop on Agentic AI for Next-Generation Software Development), Munich, ACM, 10 pages; received 2026-07-25, accepted 2026-08-20
Jagiellonian University, Krakow, and Exadel, Krakow (Jureczka, Przystalski); AGH University of Krakow and Exadel, Krakow (Paleczek); Exadel, Warsaw (Campbell)

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — BDD-Bench, a repository-level benchmark of 111 chronologically ordered instances from 5 Python repositories in which agents implement executable Gherkin specifications on an evolving codebase (lifecycle mode); 13 models compared in mini-swe-agent 2.4.5 with 3 runs each; failure taxonomy and matched golden- vs agent-prefix reruns

No SDD tool evaluated; executable BDD specifications (Gherkin with pytest-bdd or behave step definitions) are the task input. Configurations: mini-swe-agent 2.4.5 with GPT-5.5, GPT-5.4 Mini, GPT-5 Mini, GPT-5.6 Luna, GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-5.6 Terra, Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Sonnet 5, Claude Haiku 4.5, DeepSeek V4 Pro, DeepSeek V4 Flash, Gemini 3.5 Flash, Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite

Per instance: golden test patch (original Gherkin feature files and step definitions), one visible silver test patch (LLM-generated Gherkin scenarios for implied behaviour: adjacent inputs, edge cases, failure paths) and one withheld silver hidden patch; environment patch; common agent prompt naming the full-suite test command, visible Gherkin specifications as the behavioural specification, prohibited edits and completion marker

Per stage: agent receives baseline repository, environment changes, visible golden and silver test patches, repository tree and test command; changes production code only; full grading suite (new visible, prior visible as regression, new and prior hidden) runs once; pass: merge and carry forward; fail: chain stops. Benchmark construction: PR collection, executable states in Docker, chain construction (fail-to-pass), patch extraction, silver/hidden test generation with review

Benchmark construction: static review and execution testing of generated test patches; iterative review of hidden patches linked to repeated early failures or flagged by an LLM reviewer; manual spot checks of the LLM judge's failure labels. None during agent runs
Specification format only (executable Gherkin scenarios as task input and acceptance tests); no SDD workflow run

Not classifiable (benchmark; executable BDD specifications as task input). Authors' wording: 'Recent specification-driven development (SDD) workflows similarly place a structured specification before implementation ... BDD-Bench grounds the same principle in Gherkin scenarios linked to step definitions'
Existing code bases (historical states of five open-source Python repositories, evolving codebase across chained instances)

111 instances from 5 repositories (qutebrowser 39, jrnl 22, python-pptx 21, open-web-calendar 16, partcad 13), from 3,186 collected PRs/feature spans; golden production patches mean 918.7 LOC (median 362) across 26.4 files (median 16); 389 visible and 409 hidden scenarios added
Browser, journaling CLI, presentation library, web calendar, CAD framework
N/A (no participants)
None reported per model (USD 10 per-run budget and 250-step limit as constraints; budget exhaustion counted as a generation failure)

Instance-resolution rate (resolved / 111, blocked stages unresolved); production-Python-LOC-weighted resolution rate; resolved/attempted stages; full chains (of 15 repository-run pairs); means over 3 runs with min-max; matched-rerun resolution rate from golden vs agent prefix
None (direct technical-debt metrics named as future work)
None

Generation failures (step limit, cost budget, context saturation, out-of-memory, no submission); failure taxonomy of the first stopping point per chain (hidden-failure subtypes: regression, missing surface, narrow implementation, state propagation, side effect, observable contract); first stopping points by repository instance

Automatic: grading suite in reconstructed Docker images, offline, git history stripped, flaky tests excluded. Failure labels assigned by a Claude Opus 4.8 judge run through mini-swe-agent in the failing container; manual check of a random sample and a global spot-check pass, no inter-rater study

Criterion: an instance is resolved when the diff applies and one run of the full grading command passes; no criterion stated for a configuration, so quality verdict and cost verdict for every entry: no criterion stated by the authors. Values (Table 3, three-run means): LOC-weighted rate (min-max); instance rate; resolved/attempted; full chains; generation failures.

- Golden reference (lifecycle sanity check): resolves all instances
- Matched reruns (Claude Sonnet 5, GPT-5.6 Luna, DeepSeek V4 Pro, DeepSeek V4 Flash; 3 runs from golden prefix vs 3 from agent prefix per first-failing context): values only in Fig. 5; no systematic advantage for either prefix

Tasks: 111 instances in 5 chronological repository chains, lifecycle mode (classic mode for golden-prefix reruns). Configurations: 13 models in one harness. Baseline: none for the model comparison (golden reference only as sanity check). Held constant: mini-swe-agent 2.4.5, common prompt, high reasoning, max 250 steps, USD 10 per run, each model's max output tokens, 8 GB containers, 1 h per command, offline, git history stripped, unshuffled manifest. Acceptance tests: visible golden and silver scenarios, hidden silver scenarios and accumulated regression checks, fail-to-pass validated against the golden patch. Repetitions: 3 runs per model (39 runs). Human intervention: none (hung containers restarted, filesystem kept)

Claude Opus 4.8 best (45.0% instances, 29.5% LOC-weighted), then GPT-5.5 (43.5%, 26.0%) and Claude Sonnet 5 (36.6%, 24.1%); Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite lowest (1.5%, 0.2%). Seven models resolve >=85% of attempted stages; progress set by where chains first stop and by generation failures. 18 full chains across 7 configurations (16 jrnl, 2 python-pptx). Of 177 stopping points: 115 hidden-specification failures, 29 visible-test failures, 23 generation failures (cost budget 12, context 11), 10 disallowed-patch/broken-test; 0 benchmark faults; hidden failures mainly narrow implementation (36) and missing surface (34). Matched reruns: neither prefix systematically better; deeper prefixes slightly favour golden; exploratory. No significance tests; three-run ranges often overlap

Distinguished strong from weak models (1.5-45.0%), but with three runs the ranges are descriptive and overlap, so fine-grained rankings are not supported. Limitations stated: single harness; LOC weighting is not a validated difficulty measure; possible training-data contamination; GPT-5.5 generated the silver tests and was evaluated, Claude Opus 4.8 was both judge and top model (self-preference bias); only the first failing stage analysed (censoring)

Limitations: five Python repositories and two BDD frameworks, selection criteria and 50-line threshold may bias; memorisation not ruled out; one harness; three runs; LOC-weighted metric; shared-model and self-preference biases in test generation and failure judging; first-failure censoring. Gaps / future work: more repositories, languages, BDD frameworks, repetitions and harnesses; controlled studies isolating a single carried-forward defect with technical-debt metrics (defect density, duplication, maintainability); strongest agents still pass visible tests but fail withheld variants

Consistency checks: Table 3 counts add up (18 full chains across 7 configurations; 23 generation failures = 12 cost budget + 11 context); 177 stopping points = 115 hidden + 29 visible + 23 generation + 10 disallowed/broken; 115 hidden failures = 36+34+18+15+12. Text 'four of twelve Claude Opus 4.8 stopping points' vs '4 of 15 ... chains' consistent (3 chains complete). Table 3 values read from a jumbled extraction (columns split); full chains and generation failures re-aligned by row order. Benchmark and tooling at github.com/michalJur/BDD-Bench. No pre-registration. Programming language: Python (Gherkin specifications)
